hints: Focus on the words progressive wave and particle in the stem - the wave travels on but each particle only oscillates about its own equilibrium position.
Recall that a particle in a progressive wave moves with SHM, so its speed $v$ depends on its displacement $x$ from equilibrium.
Compare the two extremes of that SHM: a particle at maximum displacement is momentarily at rest, while a particle passing through zero displacement carries maximum kinetic energy.
walkthrough: In a progressive wave, energy and the wave pattern move forward, but each particle of the medium only oscillates about a fixed equilibrium position with no net drift.
That particle oscillation is simple harmonic motion, where speed is greatest at the equilibrium position and zero at the maximum displacement $x = \pm A$.
For a transverse wave this means a particle crossing its undisturbed position moves fastest perpendicular to the wave direction.
For a longitudinal wave this means a particle passing through equilibrium midway between a compression and a rarefaction moves fastest parallel to the wave direction.
The other statements fail: some transverse waves need no medium, transverse wave speeds vary between media, and neither wave type gives net particle movement.
So zero displacement corresponds to maximum particle speed in both wave types. This is option C.

options.A: Electromagnetic transverse waves such as light can propagate through a vacuum, so a medium is not required for all waves.
options.B: Wave speed depends on the medium and on $v = f\lambda$, so different transverse waves such as light and a wave on a string travel at very different speeds.
options.C: In both types the particles perform SHM about equilibrium, so speed is maximum when displacement $x = 0$ and zero at amplitude.
options.D: In a progressive wave there is no net movement of particles in either case - particles oscillate about equilibrium while energy travels forward.
